quote: Empathetic response generation, as a conditional text generation task, aims to endow agents with the ability to understand interlocutors and accurately express empathy in their communication.

We propose DIFFUSEMP, a diffusion model-based framework, for empathetic response generation. ... Experimental results on a benchmark dataset EMPATHETICDIALOGUE show that our method outperforms competitive baselines in generating more context-related, informative, and empathetic responses.

We evaluate the generated responses from four aspects: (1) Relevance: BERTScore (Zhang et al., 2020a) computes a semantic similarity between generated responses and golden references. MIScore is the likelihood of generating a context with the given response... (2) Controllability: We calculate the success rate of empathy expression with multi-grained control signals... (3) Informativeness: Dist-n calculates the number of distinct ngrams in generated responses. Self-BLEU reflects the difference of all generated responses... (4) Response Length: AvgLen represents the average number of tokens for generated responses.

Human Evaluation. We evaluate the response quality based on the following aspects: (1) Empathy reflects whether a response understands the speaker's feeling or situation and responds appropriately. (2) Relevance considers whether a response is relevant to the topic mentioned by the speaker. (3) Informativeness evaluates whether a response provides rich and meaningful information.

We recruit three third-party graduate researchers (average age 23.3) to analyze the results of various models. The response quality of all models is evaluated in terms of the following three aspects: Empathy, Relevance, and Informativeness. ... Each aspect is on a scale of 1 to 5, in which 1 is "unacceptable" and 5 is "excellent performance".
